answers.answer: For the next break, use the schedule helpers {ad.next.in}, {ad.next.in.long}, {ad.next.at}, {ad.next.seconds} and {ad.next.duration}. Inside a reply that can run at any time, wrap them in {if.ad.isScheduled:then|else}. Just before a break, use the Ad break coming event with {ad.when}. For the most recent break, use the Ad break ends event with {ad.duration}, or use {ad.last.ago} or {ad.last.at} in a command that can run at any time. None of these helpers takes an argument.
answers.quote: None of the ad helpers take an input.

answers.answer: You must already know how to edit a reply and use braces. The schedule helpers and the Ad break coming event need the Twitch permission channel:read:ads, which the first Twitch sign-in does not ask for. This is stated under Before you start. A missing permission shows in the Needs attention panel on Home. The page does not say how to grant it.
answers.quote: The schedule helpers and the Ad break coming event read your ad schedule through your own Twitch sign-in, with the Twitch permission channel:read:ads.

answers.answer: It works when the helper is replaced by a value like the Example column (12m, 15:42, 3 minutes). It has failed when chat shows the helper still in braces. Inside the check, failure shows as the second text. Schedule helpers ask Twitch at the moment the reply goes out and work in any field. Event helpers carry one ad break event and work only in a response to that event or a pipeline it starts.
answers.quote: This prints the second text when no break is planned, and also when Twitch does not answer or the permission is missing.

answers.answer: The reminder goes in an Ad break coming event response, for example 'Ad break {ad.when}. Grab a drink, we'll be right back.' It goes out once, about 3 minutes before each break, but not for a break in the first 10 minutes of the stream or without the permission. A reminder that runs on a timer uses the schedule helpers inside {if.ad.isScheduled:...|...}. The after-ad reply goes in an Ad break ends event response with {ad.duration}, which gives the length of the break that just ended. It goes out only if you are still live on the same stream.
answers.quote: For a warning just before each break, use the Ad break coming event.

answers.answer: Under Choose a reminder, I set up responses to the Ad break coming and Ad break ends events, but where to create them only appears later, under Ad break events. I had to scroll on to find it. Before you start says the permission must be granted, but no step says how, so I would guess the Needs attention panel has a fix button.
answers.quote: The three events are on the Event responses page, which is in the Build group of the sidebar.

findings: The page says 'Until the permission is granted' and names the Needs attention message 'Twitch permission missing: channel:read:ads', but no step says what to press to grant channel:read:ads, so a reader whose helpers print as typed cannot finish the task.
